citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
This facility is not providing adequate veterinary care to the animals.
A blue merle tricolor male English bull dog, named Bubba (#56422), was found to have an excessive accumulation of
greenish mucoid like material around and on both eyes. The discharge was worse on the left eye than on the right. When
the licensee was asked about the dog’s eyes it was stated that he cleans all dogs' eyes as needed but was not aware this
dog needed cleaning. However, records of veterinary exam from May 2026 noted that this dog specifically was one
requiring daily eye cleanings.
A 5 year old red and white female English bulldog, named Tanner Simpson's Blondie (#56198), was found to have a
softball size swelling on her abdomen. The lump is reducible, skin is of normal color, and is in the region below the
umbilicus where she had previously had a c-section. When asked about this lesion the licensee stated that he had noticed
a lump there before when she was nursing puppies but did not realize it had gotten so large. The licensee has not been in
contact with his AV about this issue.
The licensee is also providing a monthly dose of ivermectin to all adult dogs as prescribed by the veterinarian. The only
bottle of ivermectin on the premises has an expiration date of 05/2024. Expired medications can lose effectiveness and
are not appropriate methods of treatment or prevention.
Failure to provide adequate veterinary care and follow up with the AV can lead to unnecessary animal distress and
progression of illness. Prompt recognition and appropriate action are necessary to keep animals safe and healthy.
Each dealer shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include the use of appropriate
methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries.
Correction date: 10/14/2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Additional Inspectors:
COURTNEY JERNIGAN, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
